findings.claim: mcp_docker_prune.ps1 deletes matching exited containers unless BIOETL_MCP_PRUNE_DRY_RUN=1; mcp_docker_prune.sh defaults to dry-run unless MCP_DOCKER_PRUNE_APPLY=1.
findings.broken_invariant: Destructive agent-adjacent scripts MUST default to dry-run on every platform.
findings.observation: ps1: dryRun = env BIOETL_MCP_PRUNE_DRY_RUN -eq '1'; else docker rm -f. sh: apply default 0; docker rm only if apply==1. Different env var names.
findings.method: Read ps1 and sh prune helpers; did not execute docker rm.
findings.expected: Both helpers dry-run by default; same apply flag name.
findings.actual: Windows apply-by-default; bash dry-run-by-default; env names differ.
findings.impact: Windows MCP wrapper startup can remove exited MCP containers without an apply flag.

evidence.output: ps1 BIOETL_MCP_PRUNE_DRY_RUN opt-in; sh MCP_DOCKER_PRUNE_APPLY opt-in; skipped bioetl-* names in both

findings.acceptance: ps1 defaults to dry-run; apply requires an explicit env/flag; names documented next to sh.
findings.remediation: Invert ps1 default to dry-run; accept MCP_DOCKER_PRUNE_APPLY=1 (and keep BIOETL_MCP_PRUNE_DRY_RUN as alias if needed).
findings.automation: Unit/architecture test: ps1 source contains default dry-run before docker rm -f.
validation: ps1 does not call docker rm unless apply env is 1
